summary: Austrian occultist Rudolf Steiner founded anthroposophy, Waldorf schools and biodynamic farming on a spiritual doctrine of racial hierarchy and anti-vaccine medicine; his followers later aligned with the Nazis, and his schools still face racism and measles scandals.

evidence.note: born 1861 in a village of the Austrian empire that is now in Croatia
1902: becomes general secretary of the German Theosophical Society
1912 split, founds Anthroposophical Society, moves headquarters to Dornach, Switzerland
long segment on anthroposophic medicine, karma-based illness and anti-vaccine views
1919 first Waldorf school in Stuttgart funded by a cigarette factory head
measles outbreaks centred on low-vaccination Waldorf schools in Europe, 1999-2010
Steiner's root-race hierarchy and racist claims about non-white peoples
2017 closure of a Waldorf school in Kings Langley, England, after safety failures
organised anthroposophists praise and court the Nazi regime from 1933
SS biodynamic plantation at Dachau worked by camp inmates from 1941
2017 growth of biodynamic farming certification in the United States

notes: main_span runs from his 1902 Theosophy role to his 1925 death. covered_span ends 2017 with modern Waldorf scandals, which are direct consequences; the Marianne Williamson segment is a modern comparison and was left out of the span. The Theosophical Society is typed cult since the host treats it as one; religious-body is an alternative.
